data.title: Crude Oil Inches Higher Amid Ongoing Hormuz Crisis, Concerns Over Possible U.S. Attacks On Iran
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Giving up the gains made earlier in the session, crude oil prices have edged higher on Thursday as fears of supply disruptions increased after Iranian military continued to announce vessels hitting naval mines and catching fire while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. However, the upside movement was limited as investors assessed the surplus supply outlook projected by the International Energy Agency.

WTI Crude Oil for December delivery was last seen trading up by $0.17 (or 0.20%) at $83.43 per barrel.

The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced that two supertankers, which were escorted by U.S. jets, hit naval mines while attempting to transit through the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz which Iran has designated as an 'unauthorized route'. Reportedly, the tankers caught fire.

The information was reported by Iran's state media Tasnim as well as the Associated Press.

Both the tankers were carrying a total of more than 4 million barrels of crude oil.

The claims by Iran about vessels hitting the naval sea-mines planted by Iran have not been completely corroborated. However, market participants are pricing in supply disruptions in the near-term.

After shutting the Strait of Hormuz immediately after the U.S.-Israel joint attacks began on Iran in late February, the control over the Strait of Hormuz remains uncertain with both the U.S. and Iran making claims and counter-claims over its management.

Iran already warned fleet owners to comply with Iranian military's guidelines and not to navigate through the seaway which could expose them to mine-threats.

Yesterday, in an interview with Fox News, U.S. President Donald Trump stated that there are indications that Iran may be working to develop biological or chemical weapons since the U.S. successfully shut down its nuclear programs.

Elsewhere in the Middle East, the Saudi-led coalition stated that it intercepted a Houthi cruise missile fired towards southern Saudi Arabia.

Yesterday, the New York Times reported that Trump is weighing another round of extensive military strikes against Iran.

The report added that Israel has provided the U.S. with its intelligence findings suggesting that Iran has remade its drone and missile arsenals, and advancing its chemical and biological weapons programs.

On the inventory front, last Friday, in one of its key findings, the Paris-based International Energy Agency reported that the global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026. It added that the supply will add around 105 million barrels per day, 1.70 million bpd higher than the earlier forecast for demand.

According to the report, despite the threat in shipping the output, oil-producing gulf nations have found alternative routes to export their products to their respective destinations.

Today, at a press conference, the IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol commented that the energy world will not go back to what it was before the war started.

The U.S. dollar index was last seen trading at 103.89, up by 0.03 (or 0.03%) today.

data.title: Law firm Kirkland performed $11.8 million in free legal work for Trump administration, Democrats say
data.description:
Key points:
  • House and Senate Democrats investigating law firms' pro bono work for administration
  • Kirkland disclosed free work for US Commerce and Defense Departments
  • Probe expected to intensify following Democrats' midterm victories

By Mike Scarcella and David Thomas

US congressional Democrats probing law firms that made deals with President Donald Trump's administration said on Thursday that Kirkland & Ellis has provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to federal agencies, calling it evidence of a "corrupt bargain" with the White House.

Democrats in the House and Senate are ramping up scrutiny of nine major law firms' agreements with Trump last year to provide nearly $1 billion in free legal services in order to avoid executive orders targeting firms over their legal work, diversity policies and ​political affiliations.

Trump issued the executive orders early in his second term, part of a broader campaign of retribution against his perceived political enemies.

Kirkland performed about $4 million in pro bono work for the US Commerce Department and $2.2 million for the US Defense Department, US Representative Jamie Raskin and US senators Richard Blumenthal and Adam Schiff said in a statement.

The firm also provided free legal services to the US Postal Service and US International Development Finance Corporation, they said.

"The Trump Administration also unsuccessfully tried to involve Kirkland & Ellis in work supporting the President’s political vanity projects, such as the renaming of the Kennedy Center or supporting the illegal construction of his triumphal arch in Washington, D.C. — raising serious questions of whether other firms acceded to these demands,” the lawmakers said in a statement.

Kirkland did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump said in April 2025 that the firm had agreed to provide $125 million in pro bono work to causes he supported.

FIRM'S DISCLOSURE TO LAWMAKERS

The firm, in a November 5 letter to the lawmakers seen by Reuters, said it had billed a total of more than $18.7 million in pro bono work relating to its deal with Trump, amounting to more than 15,000 hours of attorney work for the federal government and other clients.

The firm disclosed the figures in response to requests from the Democratic lawmakers, who have vowed to continue their investigation in the next Congress. Democrats' sweeping victory in the November midterm elections will give them additional power to demand documents and testimony from the law firms about their deals and how the administration has sought to enforce them.

Raskin currently serves as the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee. Blumenthal is ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

NEGOTIATIONS WITH WHITE HOUSE

Kirkland said in its letter that it began negotiating with the Trump administration after rival firm Skadden reached its own deal in March 2025.

Kirkland said its White House agreement has had "little impact" on its pro bono work, telling lawmakers that the firm "still devotes substantial pro bono resources to interests that could be considered 'progressive.'"

The law firm is represented by prominent Washington litigator Beth Wilkinson of Wilkinson Stekloff. She did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The law firms' agreements came after Trump issued executive orders targeting four firms. The orders sought to revoke lawyers' security clearances, restrict their access to federal buildings and end US government contracts held by the firms' clients.

Four judges ⁠last year struck down the orders, finding they violated the firms' constitutional free-speech and due-process rights. The Trump administration is appealing those rulings.

data.title: Corn, wheat bounce from multi-month lows, soybeans slump
data.description:
By Karl Plume

US corn and wheat futures firmed on Thursday in a short-covering bounce from multi-month lows, while soybeans drifted lower for a fourth straight session on technical selling and as the Brazilian real weakened.

Wheat drew additional strength from worries about shipments from the Black Sea region amid an absence of diplomatic progress towards de-escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine during three-way talks between the United States, Russia and China.

Grain markets moderated after tumbling earlier this week on a strengthening US dollar, which triggered broad-based selling across commodity markets.

"Today it's just profit taking taking after corn pushed to new lows. I can argue that on the wheat side, there is a fundamental discussion because Putin basically closed the door completely on any Ukraine ceasefire," said Rich Nelson, chief strategist at Allendale Inc.

Chicago Board of Trade December corn rose 3-1/2 cents to $4.39 a bushel after earlier touching its lowest point since June 30. CBOT December wheat was up 8-1/4 cents at $5.78-1/4 a bushel after hitting its lowest since January 12 earlier in the session.

Comments after the talks by Putin, who ruled out negotiations for a Black Sea ceasefire after Ukraine destroyed part of a bridge linking Russia to Crimea, dampened hopes of progress towards de-escalation in the conflict that has stifled grain trade and crimped supplies from the region.

CBOT January soybean futures fell 9-1/4 cents to $12.07-1/2 a bushel after hitting overhead technical resistance at its 20-day moving average and breaching chart support at its 200-day average.

Soybeans were pressured by the weakening Brazilian real , which tends to trigger greater farmer sales there.

Favourable weather in Brazil has also anchored the soybean market after what is estimated to be a record US harvest.

The market has also been watching for developments in US-Chinese trade relations, in which agricultural purchases are a major issue, after discussions between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping during an Asia-Pacific summit.

data.title: License information for AI chips sent to China released by US House committee
data.description:
The US Commerce Department approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips for Chinese companies through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.

The committee said in a statement that its Republican chairman, Brian Mast, had "exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD's AI chip licenses for the People's Republic of China."

The committee said that its findings included "requested sales of 3.4 million AI chips to China, and the approval of more than 879,000 by BIS-including approvals for AI chip exports to Department of War-designated Chinese Military Companies like Alibaba and Tencent. It also includes requests by NVIDIA to depend on possible chip-smuggling fronts to facilitate their sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies."

data.title: Japanese investors sought $9.4 billion of shares in Anthropic IPO, sources say
data.description:
By Anton Bridge and Miho Uranaka

Japanese investors sought to buy more than 1.5 trillion yen ($9.40 billion) worth of Anthropic shares at its public listing this week, two people familiar with the offer said.

Japanese investors ultimately secured $2.98 billion worth of the shares, a filing showed on Thursday.

Anthropic raised $81 billion in total worldwide in what became the world's largest initial public offering on record, eclipsing SpaceX , which raised $75 billion at its listing in June.

Market sentiment has turned against AI-related firms in recent months, which sparked speculation that the Claude developer's listing would struggle to win over investors.

Anthropic ultimately priced its offering at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78.

Some Japanese investors saw Anthropic as the frontrunner among AI firms and so justified large orders, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the ​IPO publicly.

Other investors sought smaller allocations or sat out the offering altogether, seeing greater prospective returns in semiconductor stocks that have fallen sharply, such as Nvidia and Kioxia , or in waiting for OpenAI’s listing due next year, one of the people said.

More than 1,000 individuals sought allotments over 100 million yen, according to a demand survey by Mizuho Securities, part of Mizuho Financial Group , which was among the underwriters of the IPO and arranged the sale of the majority of shares sold in Japan. These applications totalled around 200 billion yen, the survey showed.

($1 = 159.5700 yen)

data.title: Wall Street slides as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI enthusiasm
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 1.79%, S&P 500 1.54%, Nasdaq 1.60%
  • Anthropic briefly hits $2 trillion in market value; shares last trading 14.3% above $83 offer price
  • Walmart down after forecasting annual sales below estimates
  • Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks lifts FY27 forecast

By Stephen Culp and Ragini Mathur

US stocks slumped on Thursday as Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revive faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.

At last glance, Anthropic shares were 14.3% above the offer price. All three major US stock indexes were off more than 1%, with the benchmark S&P 500 on track to log its fifth straight session of losses.

Anthropic's debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced late Wednesday at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly before noon. After the company's market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began to ebb.

"The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri. "That money is coming from somewhere; investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from today's trading behavior, whether it's up or down."

Even so, Ellerbroek's enthusiasm for the AI trade has waned.

"My beliefs about the growth in data center capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two," he added. "Nvidia's crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact."

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly."

Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled 9.2% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most tech stocks were lower, with Micron and Broadcom down between 1.1% and 2.0%.

Nvidia declined 1.7% after five straight sessions of losses through Wednesday, when its upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dipped 1.5%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius were down 5.0% and 7.8%, respectively.

The broader technology sector slid 1.3%.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped 5.9% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance.

Walmart was down 1% following the retail giant's disappointing annual sales forecast.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 900.74 points, or 1.79%, to 49,298.08, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 112.51 points, or 1.54%, to 7,211.12 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 391.11 points, or 1.60%, to 24,038.78.

FOCUS TURNS TO THE FED

Following Wednesday's release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in a 94.1% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the central bank's December meeting, with a small but growing 5.9% chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above the central bank's average annual 2% target.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 16 new highs and 668 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,148 stocks rose and 3,518 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.06-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted one new 52-week high and 16 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 25 new highs and 438 new lows.

data.title: Tesla Expands Cybercab To Dallas In First Move Outside Austin
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tesla first rolled out Cybercab in Austin in September.
  • Earlier this week, it was also reported that Tesla is planning a €3 billion ($3.3 billion) investment in its German plant as it seeks to expand Cybercab production outside the U.S.
  • Separately, earlier this week, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said at the Dealbook Summit 2026 that the company is looking to also make Model Y vehicles with no steering wheel or pedals.

EV giant Tesla Inc. (TSLA) said on Thursday that it has launched its dedicated robotaxi offering, called the Cybercab, in Dallas, marking its first expansion outside the city of Austin.

Tesla first rolled out Cybercab in Austin in September. The two-seater vehicle has no steering wheel or pedals and is meant solely for autonomous driving. The company has been actively scaling its production in Texas as it seeks to expand the vehicle into more cities and also to offer it to individual and fleet buyers.

While the company previously operated robotaxis in Dallas, they were limited to Model Y vehicles.

Tesla said during its third-quarter earnings call in October that it is eyeing Dallas as the next city for the vehicle’s expansion.

“We launched in Austin, but that's only because we had some cabs, and we want to swarm Austin with Cybercabs everywhere. There's no fundamental reason that we are limited to Austin,” Tesla’s VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy said about the decision.

Tesla Plans To Scale Own Fleet And Sell To Outside Customers

“We've definitely been bursting the Cybercab line to see how fast we can run it,” VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy said about ongoing production at the company’s gigafactory in Texas last month. “Right now, we're building at the rate that the Robotaxi service needs the vehicles.”

Company management also said in October that they are looking to get Cybercabs to fleet customers by the end of this year instead of deploying them into its own fleet. However, a vast majority of Cybercabs will essentially be Tesla-owned, they noted. The company has also been inviting some users to order Cybercabs for personal use in recent days. The vehicle is priced at $29,990 for individual customers, with an additional $299 monthly autonomy subscription cost.

Earlier this week, it was also reported that Tesla is planning a €3 billion ($3.3 billion) investment in its German plant as it seeks to expand Cybercab production outside the U.S. Tesla reportedly plans to construct an additional production facility at its German gigafactory with the aim of producing a million units of its Cybercab robotaxis there.

Separately, earlier this week, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said at the Dealbook Summit 2026 that the company is looking to also make Model Y vehicles with no steering wheel or pedals.

"It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people. We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got 4 or 6, or a whole family. What we plan to do is have an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people,” Musk said.

Musk is currently attempting to shift Tesla away from solely an automaker to autonomous driving and robotics as well. Cybercab is key to the pivot.

How Did TSLA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock stayed within 'bearish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'high' levels.

TSLA stock has dropped 16% year-to-date.

data.title: Meta sets $300 price on pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device: report
data.description:
Meta Platforms has set a $300 price on its upcoming AI gadget, Muse Charm, according to The Information.

To drive up consumer interests, Meta is also offering a free, 12-month 5G data plan from Verizon , the report said. Meta pushed back the release of its smartwatch until 2027 to get the Muse Charm on the market before Christmas. Earlier this year, Meta set a goal of selling 10M wearable devices during the second half of 2026 as it pushes into a market led by Apple .

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg introduced Charm during its Connect event in September. Roughly the size of an Apple AirPods case, Charm features an approximately 2-inch OLED touchscreen and built-in 5G connectivity. It expects to begin shipping the devices by early December.

Zuckerberg said Charm brings the company's Muse personal AI agent into a portable device that can be carried on a keychain, in a pocket, or with a wrist strap.

"We pack the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to," he said.

The device includes speakers, microphones, front- and rear-facing cameras, a USB-C port, and a customizable virtual Muse character, including options for its appearance and voice. Charm is designed as a dedicated interface for Muse rather than a smartphone replacement. It can connect to Muse over 5G when Wi-Fi is unavailable and is paired and synchronized through the Muse app on an iPhone or Android device. It also supports music and video playback but does not offer phone or video calling. Charm devices can interact with each other as well.

In addition to the Charm and the upcoming smartwatch, Meta is also working on an AI pendant.

data.title: ADP Acquires ZenBusiness
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

ADP has acquired ZenBusiness, an artificial intelligence-powered compliance services company that serves small businesses.

Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The human resources and payroll services company said Thursday that the acquisition will help ADP support small businesses with AI technologies.

ZenBusiness, based in Austin, Texas, serves more than 980,000 small business clients in managing payroll, tax insurance and HR needs.
